claim: Δ1-pyrroline-5-carboxylate synthase (P5CS) is vital to the synthesis of proline and ornithine.
source: The bifunctional enzyme Δ1-pyrroline-5-carboxylate synthase (P5CS) is vital to the synthesis of proline and ornithine, playing an essential role in human health and agriculture.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a fundamental property of P5CS.

claim: Pathogenic mutations in the P5CS gene (ALDH18A1) lead to neurocutaneous syndrome and skin relaxation connective tissue disease in humans.
source: Pathogenic mutations in the P5CS gene (ALDH18A1) lead to neurocutaneous syndrome and skin relaxation connective tissue disease in humans
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature in the introduction section.

claim: P5CS deficiency seriously damages the ability to resist adversity in plants.
source: P5CS deficiency seriously damages the ability to resist adversity in plants.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by citations in the introduction.

claim: P5CS forms cytoophidia in vivo and filaments in vitro.
source: We have recently found that P5CS forms cytoophidia in vivo and filaments in vitro.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and references the authors' previous work (Zhang et al., 2020).

claim: The structures of Drosophila full-length P5CS were solved in three states at resolution from 3.1 to 4.3 Å using cryo-electron microscopy.
source: Using cryo-electron microscopy, here we solve the structures of Drosophila full-length P5CS in three states at resolution from 3.1 to 4.3 Å.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by the cryo-EM data presented in the results.

claim: Distinct ligand-binding states and conformational changes were observed for the GK and GPR domains.
source: We observe distinct ligand-binding states and conformational changes for the GK and GPR domains, respectively.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by structural data in Figures 2-4.

claim: Divergent helical filaments are assembled by P5CS tetramers and stabilized by multiple interfaces.
source: Divergent helical filaments are assembled by P5CS tetramers and stabilized by multiple interfaces.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by structural analysis in Figure 1 and Figure 5.

claim: Point mutations disturbing filament interfaces prevent P5CS filamentation and greatly reduce the enzymatic activity.
source: Point mutations disturbing those interfaces prevent P5CS filamentation and greatly reduce the enzymatic activity.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figure 5D and Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: Filamentation is crucial for the coordination between the GK and GPR domains.
source: Our findings reveal that filamentation is crucial for the coordination between the GK and GPR domains, providing a structural basis for the catalytic function of P5CS filaments.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the abstract and supported by structural and functional data throughout the manuscript.

claim: Over 30 mutations in P5CS have been identified as the causes of rare diseases in humans.
source: In humans, over 30 mutations in P5CS have been identified as the causes of rare diseases (Baumgartner et al., 2000; Baumgartner et al., 2005; Marco-Marín et al., 2020; Pérez-Arellano et al., 2010; Skidmore et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: The glutamine-proline regulatory axis has been considered a promising target for cancer therapy.
source: In addition, the glutamine-proline regulatory axis has been considered a promising target for cancer therapy (Guo et al., 2020; Liu et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to prior literature.

claim: Proline synthesis is associated with plant stress resistance.
source: In plants, proline synthesis is associated with plant stress resistance (Pérez-Arellano et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to prior literature.

claim: P5CS corresponds to two individual proteins in prokaryotes and some lower eukaryotes such as yeast.
source: P5CS corresponds to two individual proteins in prokaryotes and some lower eukaryotes such as yeast.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and represents established knowledge about P5CS evolution.

claim: Bacterial GK and GPR form a complex according to kinetic analysis.
source: Kinetic analysis suggest that bacterial GK and GPR form a complex (Gamper and Moses, 1974).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to prior literature.

claim: No structure of the full-length P5CS has been solved prior to this study.
source: However, no structure of the full-length P5CS has been solved.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction to establish the novelty of the current work.

claim: The GK domain catalyzes glutamate phosphorylation.
source: The GK domain catalyzes glutamate phosphorylation, and the GPR domain catalyzes the NADPH-dependent reduction of γ-glutamyl phosphate (G5P) to glutamate-γ-semialdehyde (GSA).
evidence: This is stated in the results section describing the enzymatic functions of P5CS domains.

claim: The GPR domain catalyzes the NADPH-dependent reduction of γ-glutamyl phosphate (G5P) to glutamate-γ-semialdehyde (GSA).
source: The GK domain catalyzes glutamate phosphorylation, and the GPR domain catalyzes the NADPH-dependent reduction of γ-glutamyl phosphate (G5P) to glutamate-γ-semialdehyde (GSA).
evidence: This is stated in the results section describing the enzymatic functions of P5CS domains.

claim: The end product P5C is formed by a spontaneous cyclization reaction of GSA.
source: The end product P5C, formed by a spontaneous cyclization reaction of GSA (Figure 1A), will be used by another enzyme P5C reductase (P5CR) to produce proline.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and illustrated in Figure 1A.

claim: P5C will be used by P5C reductase (P5CR) to produce proline.
source: The end product P5C, formed by a spontaneous cyclization reaction of GSA (Figure 1A), will be used by another enzyme P5C reductase (P5CR) to produce proline.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and illustrated in Figure 1A.

claim: Increasing P5CS concentration (>1 μM) promotes the formation of filaments in the APO state.
source: Here, we observe that increasing P5CS concentration (>1 μM) also promotes the formation of filaments in the APO state.
evidence: This is an observation stated in the results section and supported by negative stain EM data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Adding all substrates increases the length of filaments at the same concentration of the P5CS proteins.
source: Our results show that the P5CS proteins can be self-assembled into filaments without ligands, and adding all substrates increases the length of filaments at the same concentration of the P5CS proteins.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by negative stain EM data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Glutamate promotes the formation and maintenance of Drosophila P5CS filaments.
source: Consistent with our previous study, glutamate (a substrate of P5CS) promotes the formation and maintenance of Drosophila P5CS filaments (Zhang et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with a citation to the authors' previous work.

claim: The electron density maps of the P5CSGlu, P5CSGlu/ATPγS, and P5CSMix filaments reached resolutions of 4.0 Å, 4.2 Å, and 3.6 Å, respectively.
source: After 3D classification and 3D reconstruction, the electron density maps of the P5CSGlu, P5CSGlu/ATPγS, and P5CSMix filaments reached resolutions of 4.0 Å, 4.2 Å, and 3.6 Å, respectively (Figure 1B–D, Figure 1—figure supplements 2–4).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by cryo-EM data in the figures.

claim: Multiple conformational states of the GK domain tetramer were obtained at 3.1–3.5 Å resolution.
source: Using a separate focused refinement strategy, we obtained multiple conformational states of the GK domain tetramer (3.1–3.5 Å) and the GPR domain dimer (3.6–4. 3Å).
evidence: This is stated in the results section describing the cryo-EM reconstruction strategy.

claim: Multiple conformational states of the GPR domain dimer were obtained at 3.6–4.3 Å resolution.
source: Using a separate focused refinement strategy, we obtained multiple conformational states of the GK domain tetramer (3.1–3.5 Å) and the GPR domain dimer (3.6–4. 3Å).
evidence: This is stated in the results section describing the cryo-EM reconstruction strategy.

claim: The N-terminus (residues 1–44) and three disordered segments in regions I, II, and III in the GK domain were invisible in the cryo-EM maps.
source: The N-terminus (residues 1–44) and three disordered segments in regions I, II, and III in the GK domain were invisible in our maps.
evidence: This is stated in the results section describing the structural features of the model.

claim: Two P5CS monomers dimerize through the interaction between their GPR domains, where the β21 at the CD interacts with the β24 at the OD of the other monomer.
source: In the model, two P5CS monomers dimerize through the interaction between their GPR domains, where the β21 at the CD interacts with the β24 at the OD of the other monomer (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and illustrated in Figure 1F.

claim: Two P5CS dimers assemble into a compact tetramer through the interaction at the GK domains.
source: Two P5CS dimers further assemble into a compact tetramer through the interaction at the GK domains.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and illustrated in Figure 1G.

claim: The P5CS tetramer serves as the building block of P5CS filaments.
source: The P5CS tetramer serves as the building block of P5CS filaments (Figure 1G).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and illustrated in Figure 1G.

claim: P5CS filament structures in all three states showed characteristics of double helix.
source: P5CS filament structures in all the three states showed characteristics of double helix (Figure 1—video 1, Figure 1—video 2).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by structural data in videos.

claim: The overall diameter of P5CS filaments in all three states is 180 Å.
source: The overall diameter of P5CS filaments in all three states is 180 Å, while the helical twist is 68° and the helical rise is 60 Å (Figure 1H).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and illustrated in Figure 1H.

claim: The helical twist of P5CS filaments is 68°.
source: The overall diameter of P5CS filaments in all three states is 180 Å, while the helical twist is 68° and the helical rise is 60 Å (Figure 1H).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and illustrated in Figure 1H.

claim: The helical rise of P5CS filaments is 60 Å.
source: The overall diameter of P5CS filaments in all three states is 180 Å, while the helical twist is 68° and the helical rise is 60 Å (Figure 1H).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and illustrated in Figure 1H.

claim: The GK domain of Drosophila P5CS is conserved with the GK protein in E. coli.
source: The GK domain of Drosophila P5CS is conserved with the GK protein in E. coli.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by sequence and structural alignments in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The GK domain exhibits a sandwich-like α3β8α4 topological folding, which is a characteristic of the amino acid kinase (AAK) family.
source: Alignments of sequences and structures indicate that their secondary structures are similar as both exhibit a sandwich-like α3β8α4 topological folding (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A), which is a characteristic of the amino acid kinase (AAK) family (Marco-Marín et al., 2007; Pérez-Arellano et al., 2010; Ramón-Maiques et al., 2002).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with citations to prior literature and supported by structural data.

claim: A structure of the GK domain with the binding of glutamate was obtained in the P5CSGlu filament.
source: We obtained a structure of the GK domain with the binding of glutamate in the P5CSGlu filament (Figure 2A)
evidence: This is stated in the results section and illustrated in Figure 2A.

claim: A structure of the GK domain with G5P-Mg-ADP was obtained in the P5CSMix filament.
source: We obtained a structure of the GK domain with the binding of glutamate in the P5CSGlu filament (Figure 2A) and a second structure of the GK domain with G5P-Mg-ADP in the P5CSMix filament (Figure 2B, Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and illustrated in Figure 2B.

claim: The GK domain structure of the P5CSGlu/ATPγS filament is virtually identical to that of the P5CSMix filament.
source: The GK domain structure of the P5CSGlu/ATPγS filament is virtually identical to that of the P5CSMix filament (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and illustrated in Figure 2—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Two ligand-binding modes (bound with Glu-Mg-ATPγS and G5P-Mg-ADP, respectively) may coexist in the active sites of the GK tetramer in the P5CSGlu/ATPγS filament.
source: We speculate that there are two ligand-binding modes (bound with Glu-Mg-ATPγS and G5P-Mg-ADP, respectively) in the P5CSGlu/ATPγS filament.
evidence: This is a speculation stated in the results section based on incomplete densities.

claim: The unexpected presence of G5P could be due to the contamination of ATP in the commercial ATPγS (80% pure).
source: The unexpected presence of G5P could be due to the contamination of ATP in the commercial ATPγS (80% pure) and all substrates were in excess during our sample preparation.
evidence: This is a speculation stated in the results section to explain the presence of G5P.

claim: Glutamate binds to the active site of GBD vertically.
source: Glutamate binds to the active site of GBD vertically (Figure 2A and C, Figure 2—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and illustrated in the figures.

claim: In the P5CSMix filament, glutamate at the binding site is converted into the intermediate G5P.
source: In contrast, G5P and ADP extend towards each other in the P5CSMix filament, and glutamate at the binding site is converted into the intermediate G5P.
evidence: This is stated in the results section based on structural observations.

claim: At ABD of the P5CSMix filament, the phosphate donor ATP becomes an ADP, associating with an Mg2+.
source: At ABD of the P5CSMix filament, the phosphate donor ATP becomes an ADP, associating with an Mg2+ (Figure 2B and D).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and illustrated in Figure 2B and D.

claim: The major motion of the GK domain occurred at the region containing flexible loops or disordered segments.
source: Superimposing the GK tetramer in the P5CSGlu filament and that in the P5CSMix filament revealed that the major motion of the GK domain occurred at the region containing flexible loops or disordered segments, whereas the α3β8α4 fold showed minor movement (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is stated in the results section based on structural comparison.

claim: The disordered segment in region II acts as a closed loop in the P5CSGlu filament, which traps glutamate in GBD.
source: In the P5CSGlu filament, we speculate that the disordered segment in region II acts as a closed loop, which traps glutamate in GBD (Figures 2C and 3A).
evidence: This is a speculation stated in the results section based on structural observations.

claim: In the P5CSMix filament, the segment in region II shifts away from the top of the binding pocket and forms an open loop, in which residue M213 interacts with G5P.
source: In the P5CSMix filament, the same segment shifts away from the top of the binding pocket and forms an open loop, in which residue M213 interacts with G5P (Figure 3A, Figure 3—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and illustrated in the figures.

claim: The closed loop has a steric clash with G5P, preventing the binding of G5P under such a conformation.
source: We notice that the closed loop has a steric clash with G5P, preventing the binding of G5P under such a conformation (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and illustrated in Figure 3—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Region II at the GK domain engages in regulating the catalytic reaction.
source: Our findings support the idea that region II at the GK domain engages in regulating the catalytic reaction.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results section based on structural observations.

claim: The helix-helix structure at region I of the P5CSGlu filament transforms into a helix-loop-helix structure in the P5CSMix filament.
source: The helix-helix structure (residues 105–113, 115–124) at region I of the P5CSGlu filament transforms into a helix-loop-helix structure (residues 105–119, 120–122, 123–128) in the P5CSMix filament (Figure 3A, Figure 3—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and illustrated in the figures.

claim: The helix-loop-helix structure is referred to as the 'hook' structure.
source: This helix-loop-helix structure is referred to as the 'hook' structure.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as a naming convention.

claim: The transformation of the hook structure results in new contact sites between neighbor tetramers in the vertical direction.
source: The transformation of the hook structure results in new contact sites between neighbor tetramers in the vertical direction, which is evidenced by a rigid density in our map (Figure 1B–D, Figure 1—figure supplements 2 and 3).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by cryo-EM density maps.

claim: The GK domain of each protomer rotates approximately 10° around its central axis, causing the horizontal compression of the GK domain dimer.
source: The GK domain of each protomer rotates approximately 10° around its central axis, causing the horizontal compression of the GK domain dimer.
evidence: This is stated in the results section based on structural comparison shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The GPR domain of P5CS belongs to the aldehyde dehydrogenase (ALDH) superfamily.
source: The GPR domain of P5CS belongs to the aldehyde dehydrogenase (ALDH) superfamily.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and represents established knowledge.

claim: ALDH family uses NAD(P)+ to catalyze the conversion of various aldehydes into their corresponding carboxylic acids.
source: ALDH family uses NAD(P)+ to catalyze the conversion of various aldehydes into their corresponding carboxylic acids.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and represents established knowledge.

claim: A conserved residue cysteine acts as the active site of nucleophile in ALDHs, forming thiohemiacetal intermediate with substrate.
source: Many studies on ALDHs have shown that a conserved residue cysteine acts as the active site of nucleophile, forming thiohemiacetal intermediate with substrate (Koppaka et al., 2012; Liu et al., 1997; Perozich et al., 1999).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with citations to prior literature.

claim: The NADPH-utilizing GPR domain of P5CS catalyzes the reverse reaction of ALDHs.
source: Curiously, the NADPH-utilizing GPR domain of P5CS catalyzes the reverse reaction of ALDHs.
evidence: This is stated in the results section based on knowledge of the enzymatic reaction.

claim: Four different binding modes of the GPR domain were observed in P5CS structures.
source: On the basis of P5CS structures, we display four different binding modes (Figure 4A–D) of the GPR domain.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and illustrated in Figure 4.

claim: In the P5CSGlu filament, no ligand binds to the GPR domain.
source: In the P5CSGlu filament, no ligand binds to the GPR domain (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and illustrated in Figure 4A.

claim: In the P5CSGlu/ATPγS filament, the density of a G5P was observed at the CD active site.
source: In the P5CSGlu/ATPγS, however, we observed the density of a G5P at the CD active site (Figure 4B, Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and illustrated in the figures.

claim: Two additional states of the GPR domain were determined in the P5CSMix filament: the NADP(H)-binding state and the NADP(H)-released state.
source: By focus refinement of the GPR dimer in the P5CSMix filament, we determined two additional states of the GPR domain (Figure 4C and D). One is the NADP(H)-binding state, when NADP(H) is present at NBD (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B). The other is the NADP(H)-released state, of which the cofactor binding site is empty.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and illustrated in Figure 4C and D.

claim: The overall structures of the GPR domain are similar in the unliganded, G5P-binding and NADP(H)-released states.
source: Conformational comparison of unliganded, G5P-binding and NADP(H)-released states shows that the overall structures of the GPR domain are similar (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and illustrated in Figure 4—figure supplement 2A.

claim: The structure of the NADP(H)-release state is identical to the unliganded state.
source: The structure of the NADP(H)-release state, which has no bound ligand, is identical to the unliganded state.
evidence: This is stated in the results section based on structural comparison.

claim: The binding of G5P to CD of the GPR domain does not lead to obvious conformational changes.
source: The binding of G5P to CD of the GPR domain does not lead to obvious conformational changes.
evidence: This is stated in the results section based on structural comparison.

claim: NBD of the GPR domain differs greatly between the G5P-binding state and NADPH-binding state.
source: We have found that the structures of CD and OD are generally consistent in those two states, while NBD of the GPR domain in those two states differs greatly (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and illustrated in Figure 4E.

claim: NBD contains consecutive alternating α-helices and β-strands (α2-β5-α2) architecture, which is known as the Rossmann-like fold for dinucleotide binding.
source: NBD contains consecutive alternating α-helices and β-strands (α2-β5-α2) architecture, which is known as the Rossmann-like fold for dinucleotide binding (Cheek et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with a citation to prior literature.

claim: Upon NADP(H) binding, the residue R525 interacts with the adenine moiety, transforming the 525REE527 loop into an ordered structure that extends the α16 helix in the Rossmann-like fold.
source: Upon NADP(H) binding, the residue R525 interacts with the adenine moiety. This interaction transforms the 525REE527 loop into an ordered structure that extends the α16 helix in the Rossmann-like fold (Figure 4F).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and illustrated in Figure 4F.

claim: The entire NBD rotates approximately 15° along the cylinder axis and slides towards CD upon NADP(H) binding.
source: Meanwhile, the entire NBD rotates approximately 15° along the cylinder axis (Figure 4—figure supplement 3A) and slides towards CD (Figure 4F; Figure 4—video 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and illustrated in the figures.

claim: The helix, when turns disordered, loses contact with the adenine moiety and then separates the cofactor from NBD via a conformational selection mechanism.
source: We hypothesize that the helix, when turns disordered, loses contact with the adenine moiety and then separates the cofactor from NBD via a conformational selection mechanism.
evidence: This is a hypothesis stated in the results section based on structural observations.

claim: A similar phenomenon of conformational change was observed in ALDH1L1.
source: A similar phenomenon was also observed in ALDH1L1 (Tsybovsky and Krupenko, 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with a citation to prior literature.

claim: The transformation of NBD contributes to bringing the nicotinamide ring of the NADP(H) close to the catalytic residue C598 of CD.
source: This transformation contributes to bringing the nicotinamide ring of the NADP(H) close to the catalytic residue C598 of CD.
evidence: This is stated in the results section based on structural observations.

claim: Conformational changes triggered by the binding of NADPH subsequently initiate the transfer of the hydride ion from NADPH to the intermediate G5P.
source: Conformational changes triggered by the binding of NADPH subsequently initiate the transfer of the hydride ion from NADPH to the intermediate G5P (Figure 4—figure supplement 3B).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and illustrated in Figure 4—figure supplement 3B.

claim: Unliganded, G5P-binding and NADP(H)-released states represent open conformation, and the NADP(H)-binding state represents closed conformation.
source: In our models, unliganded, G5P-binding and NADP(H)-released states represent as open conformation, and the NADP(H)-binding state represents as closed conformation.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as a classification of conformational states.

claim: The P5CS filament accommodates the GPR domain in both open and closed conformations.
source: We propose that the P5CS filament accommodates the GPR domain in both open and closed conformations.
evidence: This is a proposal stated in the results section based on structural observations.

claim: Recurring transformations between open and closed conformations are essential for the catalytic cycle at the GPR domain.
source: Therefore, recurring transformations between these two conformations are essential for the catalytic cycle at the GPR domain.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results section based on structural observations.

claim: Neighboring GPR dimers interact with each other and form a helical structure in P5CSGlu, P5CSGlu/ATPγS, and P5CSMix filaments.
source: In P5CSGlu, P5CSGlu/ATPγS, and P5CSMix filaments, neighboring GPR dimers interact with each other and form a helical structure.
evidence: This is stated in the results section based on structural observations.

claim: The interaction formed between F642-P644 of the contact loops in adjacent GPR domains is critical for the filamentation.
source: The interaction formed between F642-P644 of the contact loops in adjacent GPR domains, which appears as a CH/Pi interaction (Zondlo, 2013), is critical for the filamentation (Figure 5A and B, Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and illustrated in the figures.

claim: The additional interface between hook structures pairs locks adjacent GK tetramers in P5CSGlu/ATPγS and P5CSMix filaments.
source: In P5CSGlu/ATPγS and P5CSMix filaments, the additional interface between hook structures pairs locks adjacent GK tetramers.
evidence: This is stated in the results section based on structural observations.

claim: Four hooks in a GK tetramer extrude toward two opposite directions to form a 'spinning top' arrangement.
source: In a GK tetramer, four hooks extrude toward two opposite directions to form a 'spinning top' arrangement.
evidence: This is stated in the results section based on structural observations.

claim: Two pairs of hooks in a GK tetramer interact with their counterparts in two adjacent GK tetramers.
source: Therefore, two pairs of hooks in a GK tetramer interact with their counterparts in two adjacent GK tetramers (Figure 5A and C).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and illustrated in Figure 5A and C.

claim: The hook interaction forms strong contacts via hydrogen bonds (M119-R124, L121-M123) and salt bridges (E116-R124).
source: The hook interaction forms strong contacts via hydrogen bonds (M119-R124, L121-M123) and salt bridges (E116-R124).
evidence: This is stated in the results section based on structural observations.

claim: A combination of the GPR contact (for the double helix) and GK contact (for the axis) stabilizes the P5CS filament.
source: Therefore, a combination of the GPR contact (for the double helix) and GK contact (for the axis) stabilizes the P5CS filament.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results section based on structural observations.

claim: The P5CSF642A mutant proteins did not assemble into a filament with or without ligands.
source: Negative stain of the mutant P5CS showed that the P5CSF642A mutant proteins did not assemble into a filament with or without ligands (Figure 5—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and illustrated in Figure 5—figure supplement 2A.

claim: The interaction at the GPR domain interface is crucial for P5CS filamentation.
source: These results indicate that the interaction at the GPR domain interface is crucial for P5CS filamentation.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results section based on mutational data.

claim: The P5CSR124A mutant proteins formed long filaments in the APO state as well as in the presence glutamate.
source: In contrast, the P5CSR124A mutant proteins formed long filaments in the APO state as well as in the presence glutamate (Figure 5—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and illustrated in Figure 5—figure supplement 2B.

claim: Glutamate-bound P5CSR124A filaments disassembled at the initial phase of adding ATP.
source: We observed that glutamate-bound P5CSR124A filaments disassembled at the initial phase of adding ATP.
evidence: This is stated in the results section based on negative stain observations.

claim: P5CSR124A formed shorter filaments than P5CSWT when incubated with all substrates.
source: Being incubated with all substrates, P5CSR124A formed shorter filaments than P5CSWT (Figure 5—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and illustrated in Figure 5—figure supplement 2B.

claim: The interactions among the hook pairs are required for stabilizing the filament during the transformation from the P5CSGlu filament to the P5CSGlu/ATPγS filament or P5CSMix filament.
source: We propose that the interactions among the hook pairs are required for stabilizing the filament during the transformation from the P5CSGlu filament to the P5CSGlu/ ATPγS filament or P5CSMix filament.
evidence: This is a proposal stated in the results section based on structural and mutational data.

claim: The two mutants R124A and F642A exhibited a dramatically compromised activity in comparison with the wild-type P5CS.
source: We subsequently analyzed the activity of the wild-type P5CS and two mutants, R124A and F642A. The two mutants exhibited a dramatically compromised activity in comparison with the wild-type P5CS (Figure 5D)
evidence: This is stated in the results section and illustrated in Figure 5D.

claim: The integrity of filament is essential to the catalytic reactions.
source: The two mutants exhibited a dramatically compromised activity in comparison with the wild-type P5CS (Figure 5D), suggesting that the integrity of filament is essential to the catalytic reactions.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results section based on mutational and activity data.

claim: The conformation of the GK domain in the P5CSGlu filament would transform upon the binding of ATP, thereby triggering the formation of hook structure and completing the catalytic reaction.
source: Based on the similarity of sequences and structures between GK and NAGK (Marco-Marín et al., 2007), we propose that the conformation of the GK domain in the P5CSGlu filament would transform upon the binding of ATP, thereby triggering the formation of hook structure and completing the catalytic reaction.
evidence: This is a proposal stated in the discussion section based on structural similarity and prior literature.

claim: The binding of NADP+ will change the cofactor binding domain of ASADH from open conformation to closed conformation.
source: Interestingly, the binding of NADP+ will change the cofactor binding domain of ASADH from open conformation to closed conformation (Hadfield et al., 2001).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion section with a citation to prior literature.

claim: The catalytic mechanisms of the GPR domain of P5CS and ASADH have something in common.
source: Thus, we speculate that their catalytic mechanisms have something in common.
evidence: This is a speculation stated in the discussion section based on similarity to ASADH.

claim: The catalytic residue C598 of CD attacks the G5P to form the first tetrahedral thioacetal intermediate in the reaction.
source: In the GPR domain of Drosophila P5CS, our data suggest that the catalytic residue C598 of CD attacks the G5P to form the first tetrahedral thioacetal intermediate in the reaction, and then expulsion of phosphate collapses to form a stable thioacyl enzyme intermediate.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion section based on structural data and knowledge of ALDH mechanisms.

claim: A hydride is transferred to the thioacyl enzyme intermediate from NADPH, with subsequent collapse to release the product GSA.
